newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower on weak cash tone.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower on weak cash tone.

text.p: A weak tone to fed cattle prices kept pressure on CME live cattle futures, which closed at or near the day's lows, trader said. Feeder cattle also closed under pressure following live cattle with higher corn futures adding to pressure, traders said.
Live cattle ended 0.725 cent a lb lower to 0.075 higher with June off most at 64.400 cents. Feeder cattle closed 0.500 cent a lb lower to unchanged with August off most at 77.825.
Live cattle futures declined to their lowest level in five weeks as the weak tone to fed cattle that developed late last week weighed on the market, traders said.
Fund liquidation and sell stops added to the setback, especially in August which broke through support, they said.

Fed cattle prices slipped to $65 per cwt last week and packers eased bids to $64 to start this week. Fed cattle supplies are seen rising as the summer wears on. At the same time, demand for beef is expected to decline seasonally after Father's Day buying is complete, they said.
"We didn't move the (feedlot) showlist last week -- plus supplies are running about 12 percent above the five-year average for this time of year," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.

Refco, R.J. O'Brien and RBH sold June live cattle while Cargill Investor Services and Prudential Securities bought. R.J. O'Brien, Cargill and Dean Witter sold sold and buying was scattered, traders said. In live cattle options, there was trading on both sides of June 66 calls while commission houses bought August 64 puts early. Commercials were doing risk reversals, buying February 66 puts and selling 76 and buying October 66 puts and selling 70 calls. There was liquidation of the 64 June straddle late, pit sources said.
Higher CBOT corn futures and weakness in the live cattle pit weighed on feeder cattle futures which closed lower across the board, traders said.

Seasonally, corn futures often trend higher in June and this year comes at a time when feedlots appear to be full. With feedlot breakevens also being squeezed currently, demand for replacement feeders is expected to weaken somewhat, sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was inched $0.02 higher to $77.37 per cwt.
Cargill sold August late after buying on the early setback, pit sources said.
